page: Amazon Web Services r7i.large is a memory-optimized instance utilizing the x86_64 architecture and running on the Nitro hypervisor. It is powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8488C processor operating at a clock speed of 3.2 GHz. The instance is configured with 2 vCPUs, which map to 1 physical core with 2 threads per core. The processor features a 105 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for vector and matrix operations.

The instance is equipped with 16.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 5 GHz, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include any local storage, meaning all storage must be network-attached, and it features a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps. No complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included with this instance type.

Performance benchmarks show average single-core capabilities, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1691.0 and a stress-ng single-core CPU performance of 1909.48. However, multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics are relatively weak, as evidenced by a stress-ng multi-core score of 1972.48 and an uncached large-block memory read bandwidth of 10.99 GB/sec. Database operations and Redis SET performance also fall into the lower performance tiers, reflecting the resource constraints of a 2-vCPU configuration.

Qualitatively, the r7i.large offers a cost-efficient entry point for memory-bound workloads that require DDR5 memory density but do not demand high multi-core processing power. The primary tradeoff is the limited compute and network throughput relative to larger instances in the same family. It is best suited for small-scale databases, caching layers, and memory-intensive general-purpose applications.
